summary.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
summary.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

qa_highlights.question: What RTM share of the mix to expect over the next 3-5 years, and what could be the next star product after RTM (peak contracts, Green RTM, BESS)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RTM has grown about 30-35% CAGR since 2020 and expects RTM volumes to keep growing 25-30% a year, possibly exceeding DAM volumes over time; it named BESS as a potential next growth product. No numeric RTM share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX pursue a buyback given low valuations, and can IEX shareholders get a reservation in the IGX IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an IGX IPO reservation for IEX shareholders is not really possible as it is an independent IPO. It said a buyback will be considered in future, since SEBI has revised the rules for market buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: How far can exchange share of electricity grow given long-term PPAs dominate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exchange-routed share could reach about 25% of generation in five to six years, versus about 14-15% in the short-term market today, as bilateral and trader transactions shrink.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost of Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, and will MCO fees force IEX to cut fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all costs are ultimately passed to consumers, directly or indirectly, and that cost allocation and fee questions are among the open issues Grid India has raised with CERC; no timeline or answer was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline, citing the need to examine software, settlement and reliability, and compared it to availability-based tariff taking years. On share loss, management said it sees no material loss given customer integration, though it earlier estimated DAM share could fall 20-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market coupling challenge affect CERC approval of the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Goel said the legal challenge is against the order, not CERC, and that regulators and government are aligned on peak power products. He said delays are due to procedural hurdles and the products will be released over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did REC volumes fall about 80% YoY and QoQ, and why is standalone realisation per unit down sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is early in the year and that a draft allowing RPO buy-out has created market confusion, which will lift REC volumes once clarified. On realisation, management pointed to incentives in REC and Term-Ahead Market and did not reconcile the 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa comparison.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-duration 11-month Term-Ahead contract timeline, given the application is over two years old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to say when approval will come, as CERC is reviewing performance of the existing 3-month contracts and standardising longer contracts, and that contracts beyond 3 months are currently not significant in volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 0.3% social welfare gain claim and DAM coupling risk relate to customer concentration, and what is the buyer/seller concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side, buyer concentration is about 50-60% of volume, and 800-900 participants trade daily; it said concentration on the buy side has been falling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sell bids in daytime far above cleared volumes, and is solar being curtailed in the exchange?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said about 10,000-12,000 MW clears in daytime, of which solar is only about 2,000-3,000 MW, and curtailment is mainly thermal, not solar; solar has not reached the stage of curtailment on the exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How long will BESS arbitrage last and are two cycles per year feasible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two cycles are possible on 100-150 days, mainly in winter, and that arbitrage may last 3-5 years, with no definitive model; it cited FY26 arbitrage of Rs 4.81 per cycle versus Rs 5.03 in FY25 and Rs 3.80 in FY24.

risks_watch: Timing of CERC approval for Green RTM, peak power contracts and 11-month TAM; orders reserved, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending over two years.
Market coupling: Supreme Court hearing (second hearing 27 July 2026), Grid India's objections to MCO design, and management's own 20-40% DAM share-loss estimate.
Proposed RTM window cut from 15 to 5 minutes and gate closure from 75 to 50 minutes, which could reduce liquidity or affect bidding systems.
Q1 FY27 REC volume decline and a draft RPO buy-out rule that could change REC demand; realisation per unit fell sharply in the analyst's calculation and was not reconciled.
Coal exchange: registration and licensing under way, six-month transition away from e-auction, and competition from MSTC and M-Junction; fee levels not yet set.
IGX IPO (22.3% stake sale) and PNGRB stake dilution from 47.3% to 25%; IGX Q1 PAT of Rs 16 crore needs to hold.
key_quotes: And I am sure with the kind of trust which we have built over the years in these last 18 years, we should be able to retain significant market share even in the Day-Ahead Market.
So, as far as business is concerned, I do not think it is going to be significant.
So, it will be difficult for me to give any timeline on this , I can only tell you one thing that sometime in 1994-95 when availability--based tariff was first discussed in the country.
The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback, yes definitely, we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth drivers, RTM and BESS arbitrage, and the view that market coupling will have limited business impact. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on timelines for CERC approvals, market coupling regulations, the 11-month TAM contract, and the buyback, and openly declined several numeric questions.

adds.what: Indian Coal Exchange (new subsidiary, incorporated June 2026; target at least 100 million tonnes in year one)
Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products pending CERC approval; timing not committed
Carbon credit trading expected to begin in FY27 (BEE target 1 October 2026)

growth.why: No formal FY27 guidance; Q1 FY27 electricity volume rose 16% and PAT about 12%, and management expects RTM to grow 25-30% a year, but the new products await CERC approval with no committed timing and the market-coupling proposal could cut DAM share by 20-40%.
